questions.q: What is the main thing an interviewer is listening for in a scenario-based question?
options: Whether you recite a memorized textbook definition
Your reasoning process and how you arrive at a defensible recommendation, not one single 'correct' answer
Whether you can answer without pausing to think at all
Whether you agree with everything the interviewer suggests
questions.explain: Scenario questions usually have no single correct answer. The interviewer wants to see clarifying questions, reasoning, and a defensible recommendation.

questions.q: According to the four-step structure in this lesson, when should you ask a clarifying question?
options: Only if it would genuinely change your answer
Before every single scenario question, regardless of relevance
Never - clarifying questions signal weakness
Only after you've already given your final recommendation
questions.explain: The lesson recommends asking a clarifying question only when the answer would actually change depending on the response - not asking for its own sake.

questions.q: In the scenario where a client wants to close in three business days but AP approvals take five, what is the better framing?
options: Just promise the three-day deadline without changing anything
Tell the client closing quickly is impossible and refuse to discuss it further
Recognize it as fundamentally an approval-cycle speed problem, not simply a reporting deadline
Ignore AP entirely since it has nothing to do with close speed
questions.explain: A three-day close target is really a statement about how fast the underlying approval and accrual processes need to run - not just a reporting deadline to meet.

questions.q: Why is a long-tenured user's request to override journals without approval really a controls question?
options: Because it has nothing to do with Oracle Financials at all
Because journal overrides are technically impossible in Oracle Fusion
Because it is actually a request about report formatting
Because removing approval requirements undermines segregation of duties, the exact kind of control gap an audit would flag
questions.explain: The request is really about bypassing segregation of duties - a control the implementation is meant to strengthen, not preserve from a prior informal system.

questions.q: When two reports that should match don't agree and the client wants an instant answer, what should you do?
options: State plainly that you need time to trace both reports to source rather than guessing which one 'feels' right
Pick whichever report shows the larger number
Immediately delete one of the two reports
Tell the client both reports are permanently broken
questions.explain: Resisting the pressure to guess and instead tracing both reports to source - checking as-of dates, filters, and included transaction types - is the credible response.
